globalNotes: Vertically scrolling detail screen ("TREND VIEW") for the "Heart Rate Zones 1-3" metric. Dark near-black background (~#0B0F12 / #0E1316). Sticky top nav bar persists across all scroll positions: back chevron (left) + centered "TREND VIEW" title. Four screenshots are scroll positions of ONE continuous screen; overlap between them (HR Zones breakdown rows appear in both shot 1 and shot 2; "What is Heart Rate Zone Training?" header appears in both shot 2 and shot 3; zone pyramid appears in both shot 3 and shot 4) merged into single top-to-bottom order. A floating circular WHOOP logo button (purple/blue gradient ring with white "W" mark) sits bottom-right, overlapping content, fixed/floating across all scroll positions — this is the WHOOP Coach AI entry point (EXCLUDED). Status bar at very top shows 09:37 with a muted/silent bell icon, cellular bars, wifi, and battery "38". Section headings use all-caps WHOOP condensed bold style; body copy is a lighter sans with grey (#B8BFC4) text on dark cards (#1A1F24).

layout.name: Status bar

A dashed horizontal AVERAGE line spans the full width at ~1:00, with a white rounded tag labeled 'AVG' at its left end (black text). Bars: 'Jun 3 - 9' and 'Jun 10 - 16' have no/near-zero bars. 'Jun 17 - 23' is the tall bar (~1:38 total) stacked bottom-to-top: large light-grey/blue-grey segment (Zone 1, #B6C4CC) up to ~1:28, a blue segment (Zone 2, #2E9BD6) ~1:28-1:35, a green segment (Zone 3, #3FB98A) ~1:35-1:38 at the top. 'Jun 24 - 30' is a short bar (~0:13) with a light-grey Zone 1 base and a thin blue Zone 2 cap on top.

layout.name: What is Heart Rate Zone Training? card
layout.description: Full-width rounded dark card (#1A1F24). Heading 'What is Heart Rate Zone Training?' in white ~30px regular/medium. Body paragraphs in light-grey (#C2C8CC) ~24px. Para 1: 'Heart rate (HR) zone training is an exercise method that focuses on tracking your heart rate during workouts and maintaining specific HR ranges. Training within these zones helps you manage workout intensity, boosting your cardiovascular health and overall fitness.' Para 2: 'On WHOOP, your HR zones are personalized to your unique physiology, based on your heart rate reserve (HRR):' Para 3: 'Heart Rate Reserve (HRR) = Max HR - RHR' Para 4: 'Since your HRR evolves as your fitness level changes, WHOOP adjusts your zones dynamically.' Then a bulleted list: '• Zone 5 (90-100%): All out intensity', '• Zone 4 (80-89%): High', '• Zone 3 (70-79%): Moderate', '• Zone 2 (60-69%): Light', '• Zone 1 (40-59%): Very light'.
literals: What is Heart Rate Zone Training?

Heart rate (HR) zone training is an exercise method that focuses on tracking your heart rate during workouts and maintaining specific HR ranges. Training within these zones helps you manage workout intensity, boosting your cardiovascular health and overall fitness.
On WHOOP, your HR zones are personalized to your unique physiology, based on your heart rate reserve (HRR):
Heart Rate Reserve (HRR) = Max HR - RHR
Since your HRR evolves as your fitness level changes, WHOOP adjusts your zones dynamically.

layout.name: HR zone pyramid diagram
layout.description: Centered triangular/pyramid diagram inside the explainer card, 5 horizontal tiers stacked widest at bottom. From top apex to base: tier '5' red/orange-brown (#C0421F red numeral on dark-red tier), tier '4' brown/amber (#C8822E numeral), tier '3' teal-green (#3FB98A numeral on teal tier), tier '2' blue (#2E9BD6 numeral on dark-blue tier), tier '1' grey (#9AA0A6 numeral on grey base). Each tier labeled with its zone number centered.

layout.name: Why Does Exercise Intensity Matter? card
layout.description: Full-width rounded dark card (#1A1F24). Heading 'Why Does Exercise Intensity Matter?' in white ~30px. Body in light-grey ~24px. Para 1: 'Balancing time in different HR zones is key to developing your long-term fitness by making your cells stronger to facilitate more sustainable progress towards your fittest and healthiest years.' Para 2: 'Training in HR zones 1-3 helps you build your aerobic base—your body's ability to use oxygen efficiently during sustained activities like running and cycling, improving your endurance and long-term health. Prioritizing training in HR zones 1-3, rather than always pushing hard, maximizes your aerobic base-building efforts and supports your body's recovery and long-term performance.' Para 3: 'Exercising in HR zones 4-5 strengthens your heart, making it more efficient at pumping blood and adapting to intense demands. At the same time, this trains your body to perform short, high-intensity bursts, like sprinting. It improves your anaerobic capacity—the ability to sustain and recover from demanding efforts. It also increases your VO2 Max (rendered 'VO₂ Max' with subscript 2), a key measure of your fitness and long-term health.'
literals: Balancing time in different HR zones is key to developing your long-term fitness by making your cells stronger to facilitate more sustainable progress towards your fittest and healthiest years.

Training in HR zones 1-3 helps you build your aerobic base—your body's ability to use oxygen efficiently during sustained activities like running and cycling, improving your endurance and long-term health. Prioritizing training in HR zones 1-3, rather than always pushing hard, maximizes your aerobic base-building efforts and supports your body's recovery and long-term performance.

Exercising in HR zones 4-5 strengthens your heart, making it more efficient at pumping blood and adapting to intense demands. At the same time, this trains your body to perform short, high-intensity bursts, like sprinting. It improves your anaerobic capacity—the ability to sustain and recover from demanding efforts. It also increases your VO2 Max, a key measure of your fitness and long-term health.
